## Question

<div class="chapter-question">What must we specify before an apparent group pattern can be explained as the result of interacting agents?</div>

## Why this week belongs here

The course moves from model-generated responses to actors that observe one another and update over time. The sociological problem is micro-to-macro explanation, not simply whether agents can produce dialogue.

## Provisional core readings

- Barrie et al. (2026), §§10.4.1–10.4.3. [Download chapter PDF](../downloads/readings/ai-and-research-methods-barrie-et-al-2026.pdf). [@BarrieEtAl2026AIResearchMethods]
- Macy and Willer (2002), “From Factors to Actors.” [@MacyWiller2002]
- Park et al. (2023), “Generative Agents.” [@ParkEtAl2023]
- Further comparison: Chuang et al. (2024) and Ashery, Aiello and Baronchelli (2025). [@ChuangEtAl2024; @AsheryAielloBaronchelli2025]

## Planned chapter and class arc

Reconstruct the explanatory logic of classical ABMs; define state, observation, policy, network and timing; examine what memory, reflection and language policies add; compare generative-agent claims with transparent rule-based baselines.

[See the provisional Week 9 Python plan](../python/session09.qmd).
